chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from al-Ala' ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The Mudabbar (conditionally emancipated slave) is from the third.
And he (peace be upon him) said that the man may retract regarding his third, whether he had bequeathed during good health or illness.

key_terms.الثُّلُثِ: The one-third share of the estate available for bequests, distinct from the fixed shares of heirs.
key_terms.الْمُدَبَّرُ: A slave whose master bequeaths his freedom to be executed upon the master's death.

ai.seo_question: How is the emancipation of a Mudabbar funded from the deceased's estate according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies that the Mudabbar's emancipation is funded from the testator's discretionary one-third share (al-thuluth) rather than the fixed inheritance portions, a ruling applicable whether the bequest was made during health or illness. It highlights the flexibility in Islamic estate planning, allowing the master to reclaim this portion, thereby distinguishing conditional manumission from fixed bequests.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Al Husayn, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Al A’ala Bin Razeyn, from Muhammad Bin Muslim, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘Al-Mudabbar (conditionally emancipated one) is from the third’.
And he<sup>asws</sup> said for the man that he can retract with regards to his third, whether he had bequeathed during good health, or illness’.
en.sarwar: 3. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Ali ibn al-Hakam from al-‘Ala’ ibn Razin from Muhammad ibn Muslim who has narrated the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that al-Mudabbar is from one-third of the legacy.’
He (the Imam) said, ‘One can change his will about one-third of his legacy regardless of whether one is ill or in good health.’”
